glorise_reconciliation.explanation: all 21 dropped rows are Hasholt and Hagedorn, 2000 samples of the Zackenbergelven basin (Greenland); the nonglacial main table's GloRiSe subset has no Hasholt rows. Difference is fully accounted for by this single-reference exclusion; 4 of the 21 rows additionally have missing Longitude.
glorise_reconciliation.rate_units_both: the column NAME is mm/yr in both files, but the VALUES differ (see below)

rate_value_inconsistency.combined_erosion_rate_identity: VERIFIED EXACT: combined['Erosion rate (mm/yr)'] == TSS_km3_yr / Area_km2 * 1e6 for all 1078 rows (max relative deviation 1.3e-11), i.e. the published conversion TSS_km3_yr -> mm/yr over Area_km2 with an implicit 2700 kg/m3 sediment density (implied density from TSS_kg_s is exactly 2700.0 kg/m3).
rate_value_inconsistency.main_table_erosion_rate_identity: NOT REPRODUCIBLE from the combined.tsv columns: main['Erosion rate (mm/yr)'] / (TSS_km3_yr/Area*1e6) has median 2.159, IQR 1.16-8.38, max 472.3, and the ratio is NOT constant within a Basin (36 of 60 basins have a single ratio, the rest up to 190 distinct values). The ratio is strongly ANTI-correlated with TSS_mg_L (r = -0.698 in log space) but no closed form (rate = f(TSS, Q, C, Area, Season, Observation Type)) was found; a 125-combination brute-force search over the available columns found no exact identity. The nonglacial main table's GloRiSe 'Erosion rate (mm/yr)' values are therefore THE SAME UNIT (mm/yr) but a DIFFERENT NUMERIC SERIES from the bundled GloRiSe combined.tsv column of that name.
rate_value_inconsistency.consequence_for_domain_workstreams: Do NOT treat the nonglacial GloRiSe stratum as a byte-for-byte copy of GloRiSe combined.tsv. Also, main-table rate x Area is only approximately conserved within a basin (see next fields).

glorise_reconciliation.main_rate_area_exponent_note: slope of log10(main Erosion rate) vs log10(Area) WITHIN a basin: -1 would mean rate x Area is constant (flux conserved). The observed within-basin median exponent measures how the GloRiSe-level recomputation behaves.

main_rate_vs_area_regression.interpretation: pooled log-log slope of main-table GloRiSe rate on Area is ~0, so across basins the main rate is not a simple flux/area rescaling; the value stored in the main table differs from the combined.tsv column of the same name

reference_rename_in_main.note: GEMS-GLORI (Meybeck and Ragu, 1998) in the combined file became Meybeck and Ragu, 1998 in the main table

rows_only_in_main.explanation: NO main-table sample is missing from the combined file. The +1 Canfield offset is not an extra main row: the combined file contains the row USA-COL-111111-CAN1 (Colorado basin, area 6.4e5 km2) but with a MISSING Reference, while the main table assigns it to 'Canfield, 1997'. The main table therefore has 23 Canfield rows against the combined file's 22. This also explains why the combined file has 1078 rows but only 1077 non-null References.
rows_only_in_main.net_accounting: row total: combined 1078 - 21 dropped Hasholt rows = main 1057 exactly; the only per-reference offset outside those 21 is the reassigned NaN-reference row USA-COL-111111-CAN1, which changes the per-reference tally but not the row total.
